title: The Share of a Party's Outlay a Travel Protection Plans Certificate Declares
content:
These questions are answered for the share of a prepaid outlay that a Travel Protection Plans certificate declares, when its declared trip cost is corrected. The party is the party carried by the vacation package the cover was bought alongside, one of the Vacation Package Products: the adults it carries and the children it carries, which together are the party.

**Where the certificate names fewer insured travellers than the package carries in its party and the package carries no child in its party, what is the share of the outlay the certificate declares?**

It is the share the travellers the certificate names bear of that party — the insured travellers named, out of the whole party the package carries.

**Where the certificate names fewer insured travellers than the package carries in its party and the package carries at least one child in its party, what is the share of the outlay the certificate declares?**

It is the share the travellers it names bear of the adults the package carries — the insured travellers named, out of the adults alone.

**Where neither of those holds, what is the share of the outlay the certificate declares?**

It is the whole of it, 100 per cent.

## The three cases

| Insured travellers named, against the package's party | Children in the package's party | Share of the outlay the certificate declares |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fewer than the party | None | Those travellers out of the whole party |
| Fewer than the party | At least 1 | Those travellers out of the adults the package carries |
| Not fewer than the party | Either way | 100 per cent |

**What counts as the package's party?**

The adults the package carries together with the children it carries.

**Where the certificate names as many insured travellers as the package's party, or more, which case applies?**

The third. Both of the first two require the certificate to name strictly fewer insured travellers than the package's party, so a certificate naming the whole party declares the whole of the outlay at 100 per cent.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** A package carrying 4 adults and no child, on a certificate naming 2 insured travellers: the first case applies and the share is 2 out of 4, which is half. The same package carrying 3 adults and 1 child, on a certificate naming 2 insured travellers: the party is 4, the certificate names fewer, and a child is carried, so the second case applies and the share is 2 out of the 3 adults, which is two thirds.
